title: The Brain Brings Its Own Program

scenes.tts: Does the peripheral rule hold in the brain and spinal cord? Does the axon decide there too?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Brain Brings Its Own Program. An oligodendrocyte with several processes beside the closing card of the last chapter.
scenes.narration: Does the peripheral rule hold in the brain and spinal cord? Does the axon decide there too?

scenes.tts: In culture, oligodendrocytes will wrap inert plastic fibers of a suitable diameter. No axon, and still a wrap.
scenes.visual: An oligodendrocyte in a dish extends processes and wraps plain plastic fibers.
scenes.narration: In culture, oligodendrocytes will wrap inert plastic fibers of a suitable diameter. No axon, and still a wrap.

scenes.tts: In mice, Nave's group removed neuregulin one and erb bee signaling in the brain and spinal cord. Myelin still formed.
scenes.visual: Split screen: mouse spinal cord with the neuregulin and ErbB signal crossed out; its axons still carry myelin. Credit: Brinkmann and colleagues, 2008.
scenes.caption: In mice, Nave's group removed neuregulin-1 and ErbB signaling in the brain and spinal cord. Myelin still formed.
scenes.narration: In mice, Nave's group removed neuregulin-1 and ErbB signaling in the brain and spinal cord. Myelin still formed.

scenes.tts: Yet extra neuregulin from neurons could still thicken central myelin. The signal can tilt the wrap. It is not needed to start it.
scenes.visual: The neuregulin dial turns up; central sheaths thicken. Label: not needed to start, but can tilt.
scenes.narration: Yet extra neuregulin from neurons could still thicken central myelin. The signal can tilt the wrap. It is not needed to start it.

scenes.tts: So in the brain, the glial cell brings much of the program itself. Axon cues such as activity, and the caliber of the fiber, bias it.
scenes.visual: The two halves of the guiding idea: nerve, axon decides; brain, glia bring much of the program, axon cues bias it.
scenes.narration: So in the brain, the glial cell brings much of the program itself. Axon cues such as activity, and the caliber of the fiber, bias it.

scenes.tts: Zebrafish larvae have transparent spinal cords, so the first sheaths can be filmed as they form. Most early wraps are withdrawn.
scenes.visual: A transparent larva; zoom into the spinal cord where green sheaths appear and many retract.
scenes.narration: Zebrafish larvae have transparent spinal cords, so the first sheaths can be filmed as they form. Most early wraps are withdrawn.

scenes.tts: Jacob Hines, Bruce Appel and colleagues blocked vesicle release in one axon among normal neighbors. Will oligodendrocytes treat it differently?
scenes.visual: One red axon expressing tetanus toxin among green normal axons. Label: vesicle release blocked. On screen: Predict.
scenes.caption: Jacob Hines, Bruce Appel and colleagues blocked vesicle release in one axon among normal neighbours. Will oligodendrocytes treat it differently?
scenes.narration: Jacob Hines, Bruce Appel and colleagues blocked vesicle release in one axon among normal neighbours. Will oligodendrocytes treat it differently?

scenes.tts: Yes. The release-blocked axon was wrapped less often, and its sheaths were shorter. Release from the axon biases the choice.
scenes.visual: Fewer, shorter sheaths stay on the red axon; the green neighbours keep more. Label: release from the axon biases the choice.
scenes.narration: Yes. The release-blocked axon was wrapped less often, and its sheaths were shorter. Release from the axon biases the choice.

scenes.tts: In mouse cortex, stimulating neurons with light added new oligodendrocytes and thickened myelin in that circuit.
scenes.visual: Mouse premotor cortex lit by a light probe; new oligodendrocytes appear along the stimulated circuit. Credit: Gibson, Monje and colleagues, 2014.
scenes.narration: In mouse cortex, stimulating neurons with light added new oligodendrocytes and thickened myelin in that circuit.

scenes.tts: These are larval fish and mouse cortex. Whether such myelin helps adult humans learn is still open.
scenes.visual: A question mark over a human brain outline.
scenes.narration: These are larval fish and mouse cortex. Whether such myelin helps adult humans learn is still open.

scenes.tts: So the idea has two halves. In nerve, the axon decides. In the brain, the glia bring much of the program, and the axon tunes it.
scenes.visual: Closing card of the guiding idea with its two halves.
scenes.narration: So the idea has two halves. In nerve, the axon decides. In the brain, the glia bring much of the program, and the axon tunes it.
